title: a FAST, VICIOUS DASHING SLASH with a short dagger to the front (right)
physics: Physics: a savage goblin attack. A short low crouch, then the back leg explodes straight and the front foot takes ONE big step forward so the whole body shoots low and forward. The dagger, gripped in the LEFT (near) hand, cuts across from high-back to low-front in one stroke and leaves a bold crescent smear trail bigger than the goblin's body. No pauses, no second cut. Exaggerate the poses about 25%. Snarling, teeth bared, eyes glaring at the target the whole time.
poses: Ready stance exactly like #1: low aggressive crouch, the dagger low in the LEFT hand.
Anticipation: crouching even lower, weight on the back (left) leg, the dagger pulled back high behind the shoulder, the free right hand clawed forward, snarling.
Dash start: the back leg pushes, the front (right) foot lifts and moves forward, the body leans low and forward, the dagger still cocked back.
Dash: the front foot lands one big step forward, the body is low and stretched forward over the front knee, the dagger at its highest point behind.
SLASH: the dagger arm whips from high-back to low-front; draw a bold pale crescent smear arc along the whole path, larger than the body.

IMPACT: the dagger arm fully extended forward and down at the end of the arc, deep wide stance, torso bent over the front knee, ears and scarf whipping forward; the tail of the smear is still visible, fading.
Follow-through: the dagger continues low past the front knee, the body sinks slightly lower; no smear.
Recovery start: pushing back from the front leg, the dagger rising to hip level, still glaring forward.
Recovery: the front foot is pulled halfway back, the body rising into a crouch.
Recovery: the front foot almost back in place, the dagger lowering in front of the hip.
Recovery: settling into the ready crouch, ears and scarf settling.
Ready stance like the first pose.
rules: The dagger stays in the goblin's LEFT hand (the near hand) in every frame, and moves smoothly from frame to frame — it never jumps or switches hands.
The back (left) foot stays at EXACTLY the same spot on the ground in every frame. Only the front (right) foot moves: one step forward in the dash, back in the recovery.
3/4 view facing right like #1 in every frame, never toward the camera.
After the impact the dagger only goes down and back to the ready position — it never swings forward again.
Expression: a fierce snarl with bared teeth in every frame; no smile, no blush.
